In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the work activity of small teams in order to design collaborative technology.
understanding the nature of collaboration, in particular, the role of the shared drawing space in collaborative work.
the development of collaborative technologies that support the work of small groups of collaborators.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the design of collaborative technology should support the use of the drawing surface and hand gestures as well as the fluent mix of activity around the shared drawing space.

the design of collaborative tools should take into account the importance of gesture, the process of drawing as well as its products, the role of the drawing surface as a resource, and the importance of the orientation among the collaborators.
the design of collaborative tools should be informed by a detailed understanding of the collaborative work activity they will support.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the collaborative work we observed was characterized by a complex mix of activities, and that this complexity was supported by the physical environment.
collaborative activity is not just the sum of individual activity.
we have found that the work activity of small collaborative groups has a rich and complex structure, and that this activity can be effectively supported by technology.
The main takeaway from our work is that
collaborative work is a rich and complex activity that is not well understood.
the design of collaborative technology needs to support the collaborative work of groups in the ways that the physical environment supports it.
there are many aspects of collaborative work that cannot be captured in the final product of the work.
